summary: Live-launch canary: this Claude CLI worker session was started by the Task MCP launcher, claimed CLAUDE_TASK_MCP_LIVE_LAUNCH_CANARY_B313_V1 via taskctl claim-start, continued execution past the claim-start boundary, created isolated evidence artifacts, ran validation, and returned the task to Codex review. No product source was mutated. No shell invocation was used. The full worker lifecycle (claim -> guard -> write -> test -> review) completed in one uninterrupted session.

lifecycle_evidence.process_launch_vs_completion_distinction: claim-start only transitions task to processing/claimed; the worker must continue in the same session to create artifacts, pass validation, and call taskctl review to enter the review state. These are distinct lifecycle events: launch (claim-start) != completion (review).

process_launcher_observations.build_worker_prompt_function: process_launcher.py:build_worker_prompt() generates the exact CLI prompt injected into this session; its template matches the prompt I received
process_launcher_observations.shell_false_invariant: ProcessManager.launch() passes shell=False to subprocess.Popen; no shell interpretation of worker commands
process_launcher_observations.dual_env_gate: AIWORKHUB_ALLOW_LAUNCH=1 and AIWORKHUB_ALLOW_WRITES=1 must both be set for real process launch
process_launcher_observations.launch_implemented_true: LAUNCH_IMPLEMENTED=True constant confirms real process launch is implemented (not a stub)
process_launcher_observations.audit_log_append_only: process_events.jsonl is O_APPEND only; never rewritten
process_launcher_observations.claim_start_not_completion: task card worker_status transitions: unclaimed->claimed (claim-start) then claimed->review (taskctl review); launch event != completion event

context7_usage.reason: Pure repo-local canary over existing process_launcher.py and taskctl infrastructure. No external library/API question open.
